objective.statement: Read 5/4, 7/4, 5/8 and 7/8 as combinations of groups of two (or four) and three beats.
successCriteria: I can tell an irregular time signature from a regular one.
I know the upper figure counts the beats and the lower figure names the beat.
I know the same signature can be grouped in more than one way.

explanation.text: So far every bar you have met had beats that were all alike: two, three or four of them, simple or compound. A time signature with five or seven beats in a bar is called irregular, because its beats cannot be shared out evenly. Instead the bar breaks into smaller groups of two and three beats (a group of four is also possible: seven beats may be 4 + 3). At Grade 5 the irregular signatures are 5/4, 7/4, 5/8 and 7/8.

Read them as you read any time signature. The upper figure says how many beats are in a bar; the lower figure says which note value is one beat: 4 is a crotchet, 8 is a quaver. So 5/4 is five crotchet beats, and 5/8 is five quaver beats. A bar of 7/8 holds seven quavers.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 5/4. The first has five crotchets. The second has a dotted minim followed by a minim.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet, crotchet, crotchet, crotchet, crotchet. Bar 2: dotted minim, minim.

explanation.caption: Both bars of 5/4 add up to five crotchets. The second bar shows a 3 + 2 grouping.

explanation.text: Some questions list regular and irregular signatures together: work out the bar length first, and look for dotted beats or three-note beams (compound time) before you decide. A time signature does not say how the beats are grouped. Five beats may fall as 3 + 2 or 2 + 3; seven beats as 2 + 2 + 3, 3 + 2 + 2, 2 + 3 + 2 or, with a group of four, 4 + 3 or 3 + 4. The composer shows the grouping with note lengths and beams, and a piece usually keeps the same grouping from bar to bar.
To find an irregular signature, add up one bar in the smallest beat: five beats or seven. The upper figure is 5 or 7; the lower figure is the value you counted in.

independent.prompt: Which of these is an irregular time signature?

6/8.reason: 6/8 is compound time: its beats are all alike (duple). Irregular time has five or seven beats, made of twos and threes.

3/4.reason: 3/4 is simple time: its beats are all alike (triple). Irregular time has five or seven beats, made of twos and threes.

Follows Grade 5 outcome 1 and First Steps Grade 5 section 1 (p. 105, read in the PDF): five or seven beats; bars are combinations of two- (or four-) and three-beat groups (the book's own 7/8 example is 4+3); only 5/4, 7/4, 5/8 and 7/8 at Grade 5.
